Just got around to updating my log book and notes, so why not post a trip report!

Ended up with a few weeks since my last flight and work is threatening to make it difficult to do any flying this month. Called up my brother and asked if he wanted to go on a pancake run. Had two options for planes the morning that worked - the C152 or the C182. Opted to take the faster plane and invite my little nephews to come along.

Sunday morning was severe VFR conditions. Clear skies, 6kts. It had been a few weeks since I'd driven my car, and discovered the battery was low. My Bride grumbled, but was willing to drop me off and pick me up later in the day - but I needed to be back by noon for a birthday party. The last person to fly the 182 put the keys in the office, so ended up waiting for the keys. Plane got a very detailed pre-flight as I searched for the keys, finding all the required paperwork, including a bit hidden away in a glove box. An instructor showed up, unlocking the FBO just as I was about to scrap a perfectly good day of flying. A late start, but still doable.

Picked up flight following, and got cleared into MSP's bravo airspace, and headed directly to St. Cloud. Picked up my brother and the kids at one of the local FBO. These kids were excited, and it was the first time my brother had been in a 'roomy' GA aircraft. Way more comfortable than the little two seater Cessna. As we taxied out to the runway, one of them said it seems just like driving a car. Moments later, we roared down the runway and they were cackling with glee.

Turbulence was reported, but the flight was pretty smooth. There were a few bumps as we departed the airport, but nothing that would create a cleanup situation. Picked up flight following again, picking an altitude a couple thousand more than I planned, just to stay in radar services the entire way. Made my first mistake on the trip. As ATC handed me off from one frequency to the next, I repeated back 121.5 rather than 121.05. Plugged it into the Garmin 650, started to call out my call sign, and realized I was on guard (before dozens announced I'd screwed up). Doh! Flipped back to the previous frequency and confirmed I was suppose to be on 121.05. Much better.

Things were crowded as I got near Brainerd. Lots of VFR traffic working their way to the air show mecca. I pulled out my airport diagram and realized there was no tower. Doh! The FF folks pointed out a half dozen bogies, including a flight of RVs. Don't think any of us saw each other till we got in the pattern, but we were all chatting altitudes and landmarks.

Wings Cafe was right on the field. Did the long taxi down the 6500', chocked the wheels, and went in for some breakfast. Kids devoured the pancakes, my brother and I did the wild rice porridge. (yum) Kids hit the restroom while I checked the weather, and we climbed back into the airplane. I did have the boys return the chocks - they seemed very pleased with the task and wondered why the jet had not put theirs back. Discovered my tablet had shut down from the heat. Should not have left it in the sun. Pulled out my paper sectional, handed it off to my brother, and departed. Tablet rebooted, but really was not needed for anything but the kid's amusement.

From the departure, I knew I'd need altitude if I wanted radar coverage. Climbed to 6500 to also stay clear of all the traffic below us. Wind was working in our favor and made an uneventful landing back in St Cloud, dropping off my passengers. Climbed again to get into radar coverage and out of traffic. Silly easy to to in an almost empty 182. I was expecting ATC to let me into bravo, when some rerouting made it clear I'd be going underneath it. Ended up going from 6500 to 3500, then 2500 very quickly. With the tail wind, I suspect that was the fastest I've ever gone from Buffalo / Maple Lake to the Minnetonka area, which was good, since I was running out of time.

Switched to KFCM tower frequencies when I had a visual on the airport, and they routed me to 28R for a full stop. Set up in the pattern but was starting to get buffeted by the winds. As the mains are coming down, a gust hits hard. Things were not stable, and fearful of porpoising, I went full power and told tower I was going around. New winds announced, which matched the realities I just felt. Taxied back, parked, and my Bride called saying she was 5 minutes away from pickup.
Trip report: KFCM > KSTC > KBRD pancake run

When trolling engages in either direct threats to other people or direct planning/inciting crime.

For instance: "Some one should shut him up permanently". Borderline, but legally defensible. "I'm going to find you and shut you up permanently." Direct threat that are definitely not protected.

Another: "Robbing liquor stores has more job security than I have". Protected. "Here's the address of a liquor store. Let's rob it and fsck up the owner." Absolutely not protected.

To me, trolling is intentionally saying something with the singular intention of upsetting others. While people who use their right to free speech may upset people in the course of spreading their message, it's not their intended goal. They want to spread an unpopular message, regardless of if it's going to upset someone, because they think it is the right thing to do.
